blocks.text: LLaMA Factory is a fine-tuning framework distinguished by its web-based user interface, letting a training run be configured and launched through dropdown menus and form fields rather than writing code or editing a YAML file, a further step in accessibility beyond the config-file approach covered in the previous Axolotl topic.
This topic covers what the web UI actually offers, the range of models and methods it supports, and who benefits most from a graphical fine-tuning workflow.
1. A Web UI for Fine-Tuning
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472613827-168391696.png

Where Axolotl, covered in the previous topic, lowers the barrier from writing training code to writing a YAML file, LLaMA Factory goes a step further, providing a browser-based interface where model choice, dataset, training method, and hyperparameters are all set through visual controls.
2. Configuring a Run Through the Interface

blocks.alt: Configuring a Run Through the Interface
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472613828-703245571.png

A typical session involves selecting a base model from a dropdown, choosing or uploading a dataset, selecting a fine-tuning method, and adjusting hyperparameters through form fields, then starting the run directly from the browser, with training progress and logs displayed in the same interface.
3. Supported Fine-Tuning Methods
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472613828-443291894.png

LLaMA Factory supports the same range of fine-tuning strategies covered in earlier modules, full fine-tuning, LoRA, QLoRA, and freeze tuning, a technique that trains only a subset of layers, letting a user compare different approaches without needing to know the underlying implementation details of each.

blocks.text: 4. Support for Alignment Training Stages
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472613829-64818124.png

Beyond supervised fine-tuning, LLaMA Factory also supports the alignment training stages covered in the earlier Alignment Training module, reward model training, PPO, and DPO, all configurable through the same web interface rather than requiring separate TRL code, covered in an earlier topic, to be written by hand.
5. Broad Model Family Support
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472614371-510370599.png

LLaMA Factory supports a wide range of open model families out of the box, generally broader than the narrower, deeply optimized set Unsloth targets, covered in an earlier topic, trading some of Unsloth kernel-level speed optimizations for wider applicability across different base models.

blocks.title: Breadth versus depth of optimization is a recurring tradeoff
blocks.content: Across this module, frameworks with broader model support, LLaMA Factory and Transformers among them, generally trade away some of the specialized speed gains that narrower, deeply optimized tools like Unsloth achieve for their specific supported models.

blocks.text: 6. Who Benefits Most From a Web UI

blocks.alt: Who Benefits Most From a Web UI
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472614372-472896089.png

A web UI lowers the barrier for users less comfortable writing Python or editing YAML directly, letting them run standard fine-tuning workflows through a familiar visual interface, experienced practitioners can still benefit from the same interface for quickly prototyping runs before moving to code-based tooling for more customized needs.
7. The Underlying CLI Still Exists
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472614373-844168799.png

Every run configured through the web interface corresponds to an equivalent command line invocation under the hood, so a user who starts with the UI for convenience can later move to the CLI directly for automation or scripting, without needing to switch to an entirely different tool.
8. LLaMA Factory vs Axolotl

Both LLaMA Factory and Axolotl, covered in the previous topic, aim to reduce the amount of custom code needed to run a fine-tuning job, LLaMA Factory web UI adds an extra layer of accessibility beyond Axolotl YAML configuration, at the cost of being somewhat less suited to fully scripted, automated pipelines compared to a pure config file or code-based approach.
9. When LLaMA Factory Is a Good Fit

LLaMA Factory tends to fit teams or individuals who want to quickly experiment across many models and methods through a visual interface, particularly useful for prototyping and comparing options before committing to a more code-driven, automated pipeline for a production training setup.
Worked Example
A researcher wants to quickly compare how a model performs after SFT alone versus SFT followed by DPO, covered in earlier topics, without writing separate training scripts for each stage.

Using the LLaMA Factory web UI, they configure and launch the SFT run first, then reload the resulting checkpoint and configure a DPO run against it, moving through both stages entirely through dropdown selections and form fields, and later export the equivalent CLI commands to formalize the same two-stage pipeline for repeatable, scripted runs.
Common Mistakes

items: Relying solely on the web UI for a production pipeline that really needs full automation and version-controlled configuration
Assuming broader model support means the same level of kernel-level optimization Unsloth provides for its narrower supported set
Not exploring the underlying CLI commands the UI generates, missing an easy path toward scripting and automation
Choosing LLaMA Factory purely for its interface when a team is already comfortable with, and better served by, direct code-based tooling

blocks.text: Practice

For a fine-tuning workflow you are designing that spans multiple stages, SFT followed by a preference optimization method, sketch how you would configure each stage through a web UI style workflow, then identify what the equivalent CLI commands would need to specify for each stage.
Key Takeaway

LLaMA Factory provides a web-based interface for configuring and launching fine-tuning runs across a broad range of model families and methods, including full SFT and alignment training stages like PPO and DPO, lowering the barrier to experimentation while still exposing an equivalent CLI for teams that want to move toward automated, scripted pipelines.
